To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ICD‐ and DSM‐IV networks differ in terms of the number of nodes (symptoms) they include, the level of connectivity (number of connections between symptoms), and the level of clustering (how symptoms group together).

(i) The DSM‐IV‐R and ICD‐10 diagnostic networks differ in terms of number of disorders, clustering and connectivity; (ii) Both networks show features characteristic of a small‐world network; (iii) Both networks have similar high centrality nodes; and (iv) The DSM‐ IV‐R network structure follows comorbidities rates more closely than does the ICD‐ 10 network.

(a) the ICD‐ and DSM‐based diagnostic networks differ in terms of number of nodes, clustering, connectivity, and centrality; (b) both networks are small‐world; and (c) the DSM‐network follows the comorbidity rates better than the ICD network.
